args.summary: Run GCSP through an independently hosted frontend and backend API
args.description:
Local migration Epic: `E1`.

**Intent:** As the team maintaining GCSP, we can release a static frontend independently of the backend while users retain the agreed authenticated journeys and the new app preserves its state between ordinary restarts. Initial cutover may reset the agreed legacy operational state.

### decided / proposed scope

- Publish the complete GCSP frontend as static HTML, JavaScript, CSS and assets. Move request-time asset preparation into the frontend build. The backend supplies APIs and application services rather than employee/presenter HTML pages.
- Give every frontend consumer one consistent API configuration and request boundary. Reuse the compiled Angular bundles across environments, supplying public API/OIDC settings at deployment without recompiling Angular. Keep provider/client secrets and private service configuration on the backend. Public frontend configuration may identify the application API, OIDC issuer/public client/scopes and presentation settings; Angular holds only the user credentials/tokens required by the agreed public-client flow, never a client secret.
- Replace HTML-request session redirects and presenter-cookie setup with Angular OIDC sign-in, bearer-authenticated API context and dedicated presenter-role operations. Enforce authorization, eligibility, ownership and business transitions on the backend; remove presenter principal impersonation.
- Define replacement deep links, refresh, role navigation and brand/context handling. Newly issued offer links require sign-in/return and ownership checks; legacy GCSP URLs/API consumers need no backward compatibility. Update shared launcher/handoff links while preserving Used Cars. Define asset caching for independent releases.
- Retain Render and PostgreSQL. Define separate static/API services in the same repository's Render blueprint, using existing Render hostnames where feasible, with bearer requests, exact-origin CORS and the test-provider redirect arrangement proved on HTTPS. A purchased domain is a fallback only if needed. Gary creates the dev-branch Render environment with its own PostgreSQL database; prove reset/connection isolation from the running environment.
- Record frontend/API compatibility, independent release order and Gary's merge-triggered final switch so a frontend rollout does not depend on bundling its pages into the API deployment. Final interruption is acceptable and the old deployment need not be retained.

### acceptance

1. The frontend build can be served by a static host without a Node frontend process or per-user HTML generation. Static assets contain no private employee or presenter state.
2. Supported application reads and commands use the backend API. No frontend code accesses PostgreSQL, upstream operational services or server secrets directly. Backend authorization still refuses an unauthorized request made outside the UI.
3. OIDC login, logout/expiry, bearer-authenticated context, employee/Greg/presenter separation and newly issued offer-link ownership work under the chosen deployed origins, including direct entry and refresh. Renew where supported; otherwise sign in again and return to the authorized page with saved progress. Unfinished orders require confirmation without automatic submission after recovery. Sign-out clears app authentication and ends the provider session where supported; the next login can choose another account. Presenter controls grant no employee/Greg impersonation.
4. The agreed route inventory resolves to the correct frontend state. Invalid routes, unavailable APIs and expired sessions have usable recovery states; API errors never turn into an HTML fallback response.
5. Frontend and API artifacts can be built and released separately. Different public API/OIDC configuration works with unchanged compiled Angular bundle hashes. Demonstrate compatible releases with retained source/reference inputs and rehearse the agreed fresh-state cutover. New-app saved state and newly issued links survive ordinary compatible releases/restarts; the one-time legacy operational reset is explicit. Hand over Gary's merge into `gcsp-poc` and resulting Render replacement build; no old-deployment retention or rollback demonstration is required.

### validate

Use the existing route inventory and manual acceptance scenarios. Exercise the selected HTTPS topology in supported browsers, including Safari and private browsing, rather than relying on loopback or CORS inspection alone. Cover login/context, dedicated presenter controls/reset, saved preferences, manual claims, signed-in offer entry/decisions and Greg's operations; retain server authorization checks. Record actual results, failures and unrun cases. E2 supplies Angular-specific routing acceptance when its screens replace the current frontend.

**Boundary:** backend language conversion and adapter completion belong to E3. E1 introduces no microservices, repository split, database migration or Cloudflare move. It preserves existing behaviour and does not absorb performance tuning or new product features.

## Shared confirmed migration contract

- Scope is GCSP only. Preserve implemented capabilities, business outcomes and visual design at the exact `gcsp-poc-dev` implementation-kickoff SHA, apart from the agreed OIDC/presenter changes. Record that SHA, routes/jobs/capabilities, retained artifact identities, workload and visual references at kickoff. Preserve Used Cars and shared consumers; unfinished backlog and later product changes stay separate. Legacy GCSP URL/API compatibility is unnecessary.
- Angular 21 owns screens/navigation and calls a separately buildable/deployable Java 21 / Quarkus 3.x API. Runtime/jobs use Java without invoking Node business execution; offline generators/trainers may remain JavaScript. Pin compatible exact versions, reconcile BMW standards when supplied and keep interim Render delivery. One repository and Render blueprint define separate frontend/API artifacts. Reuse unchanged compiled Angular bundles with deployment-supplied public API/OIDC settings and no embedded secrets.
- Use real test OAuth 2.0/OIDC browser login and JWT access tokens sent as `Authorization: Bearer`; backend validates signature/issuer/audience/lifetime and enforces roles/ownership. BMW activation follows available contracts/access. Employees and Greg act only through their own logins. Presenter controls clock/releases/scenarios/resets/faults/retry plus read-only inspection such as outbox/comparison; no impersonation or employee/Greg commands. Greg retains comparison commands.
- Renew authentication where supported; otherwise sign in and return to the authorized page with saved progress. Never automatically submit an unfinished order after recovery; require explicit confirmation. Sign-out clears app authentication and ends the provider session where supported so another account can sign in. New emailed offer links require sign-in/return and employee ownership.
- Gary creates the isolated Render dev environment from `gcsp-poc-dev`, with its own PostgreSQL database. Prefer existing hostnames without buying a domain; prove HTTPS/CORS/OIDC/link topology. Minimize cost and show measured options before any spending change; no tier is selected. Prove existing scenario/comparison sizes with a few simultaneous demo users.
- Retain source corpus, policy/reference versions, reusable trained models and agreed baseline comparison artifacts. Legacy employee/scenario state, sessions, active offers/orders, old emailed links and operational learning/comparison history may reset at final switch. Replacement-app state and newly issued links must survive ordinary compatible releases/restarts. Never reset the running app's database from dev.
- Select backend adapters at deployment/startup. Reuse existing ports; separate provider transport/shape/authentication and demo preparation from application services. No silent synthetic fallback, fabricated source facts or per-employee outcomes. Keep canonical PolicyService, exact vehicle identity, provenance, pinned quotes, exclusive authority, durable receipts, retries and truthful pending/refused/uncertain outcomes. Numeric tolerances must preserve displayed values, eligibility, ranking/tie-breaks and allocation/order outcomes.
- Delivery order: foundation → real sign-in/account → Buddy matching → real test email → signed-in acceptance → order/status with local substitutes first; then remaining capabilities and the remote/full transactional substitution proof before final acceptance. Both proofs use real test OIDC and actual email delivery through the configured mail adapter to an agreed test recipient. Captured outbox alone is insufficient. Test substitutes do not establish unavailable live BMW integration.
- Complete and validate continuously, with coherent commits and no interim human review gates. Gary checks the whole hosted dev build at the end, then performs the merge into `gcsp-poc` that triggers Render replacement. Downtime and immediate retirement are acceptable; no old-deployment retention, job-draining or deployment rollback rehearsal is required. Database transaction rollback and normal replacement-app recovery remain required.
- Settle persistence design early against Russell's FUCQ-408/FUCQ-409–425 objectives; deliver relevant persistence changes with Java. Completing the whole Node refactor is not a gate. Existing native acceptance/claims stay fixed and optional tuning remains separately prioritized. This publication does not modify those issues or claim Java work satisfies Node-specific acceptance.

## Binding delivery and experience references

Read `docs/gcsp/README.md`, `docs/gcsp/demo-brief.md` (binding adapter/purpose boundaries), `docs/gcsp/build-rules.md` (including demo delivery/scope control), `docs/gcsp/experience-quality.md`, `COMPONENTS.md` and `docs/gcsp/technical-readiness-2026-11-05.md` before pickup. Preserve the kickoff implementation's visual design. The existing reference in `docs/gcsp/screens/README.md` governs shell/header/sidebar/palette; use the current shared components and recorded approved implementation references for the body. UI and visible backend changes need actual rendered desktop/narrow, Safari/private-browsing, keyboard/focus and relevant CSP/accessibility evidence. Record affected loading/empty/unavailable/denied/stale/pending/success/expiry states as applicable; backend decision changes need corresponding presentation evidence. Shared changes require relevant Used Cars checks.

Reuse meaningful existing service/HTTP/journey/adapter scenarios; avoid a new generic validation framework. Run integrated Angular journeys against the actual Java API and native PostgreSQL for transaction/concurrency/restart evidence. Record real failed, skipped and unrun checks and limitations. Builds, fixtures, source inspection and diagrams do not establish integrated acceptance or live BMW access. Triage defects under the standing policy and keep claimed acceptance fixed.

Publication creates backlog records only: no claim, implementation, provisioning, deployment, reset, test email or final merge is started. Verify actual contracts/interfaces, active ownership and concrete technical blockers, then size or split oversized work before pickup. Jira dependency links alone are not admission gates. No estimates or assignments are invented here.

## Source and traceability

Refined with Gary Carter on 13 November 2026. Source revision: `23f6ce3313916f41264c3157d70188d79287d511` (authoring evidence, not the future implementation freeze).

- [Epic scope](https://github.com/garyscarter-ibm/vehicle-matcher/blob/23f6ce3313916f41264c3157d70188d79287d511/docs/gcsp/angular-api-adapter-epic-proposals-2026-11-13.md)

args.summary: Run the GCSP backend on Java 21 and Quarkus 3.x with replaceable adapters
args.description:
Local migration Epic: `E3`.

**Intent:** As the team maintaining and integrating GCSP, we can operate its backend on the requested Java platform, replace external providers through explicit adapters, and preserve business decisions, reference data and working journeys behind the agreed Angular-facing API contract.

Adapter completion and proof are part of this Epic's completion contract. The workstream below retains the former standalone adapter Epic's coverage and evidence requirements; a successful language port alone does not satisfy them.

### decided / proposed scope

- Implement the GCSP backend runtime in Java 21 with a pinned Quarkus 3.x release. Include the supported API routes, application services, policy/recommendation/allocation logic, repository, provider adapters and existing clock, notification and job responsibilities. Maintain static frontend delivery under E1; Quarkus does not become an HTML-rendering frontend.
- Establish a capability/behaviour baseline from the supported Node implementation and define the replacement Angular-facing API contract. Legacy paths, methods and payload shapes need no backward compatibility. Preserve business meaning, identifiers/reference integrity, dates, role/resource checks and version/command guarantees. Record the intentional OIDC bearer-authentication, signed-in offer-ownership and presenter changes; they do not authorize unrelated product changes.
- Retain source corpus, policy/reference versions, reusable trained models and agreed baseline comparison artifacts with their identities/hashes; use PostgreSQL as the durable store. Legacy employee/scenario state, sessions, active offers/orders, old emailed links and operational learning/comparison history may reset at cutover. Prove exclusive claims/holds, pinned new-app policies/quotes, idempotent commands, pending outcomes and recovery. Use the separate development database and rehearse fresh-state cutover without touching the running app's operational data. Old pending work need not be drained or migrated before Gary's immediate replacement.
- Translate decision logic with shared reference inputs and expected outcomes. Define numeric tolerances that preserve displayed values, eligibility, ranking/tie-breaks, explanations and allocation/order outcomes. Retail's JavaScript implementation remains supported; cross-language parity evidence replaces assumptions that Java can import the existing JavaScript modules.
- Replace Node-specific runtime facilities where they are used, including comparison workers and filesystem-backed corpus/model reads. Preserve the supported capabilities and lifecycle; introducing an autonomous scheduler or new event platform is separate scope.
- Carry the existing adapter boundaries into Java interfaces and trusted Quarkus composition, completing the provider-selection and demo-preparation gaps identified below. A temporary Node coexistence route can support migration, but the final in-scope backend runs in Java; permanently forwarding business operations to Node does not complete the port.
- Supply a reproducible portable JVM artifact, external runtime configuration, health/readiness and Render deployment path. Run on Render and demonstrate startup outside it; list the service capabilities, reference artifacts and identity/platform settings needed for BMW activation. Reconcile further BMW standards when Gary supplies them. The running GCSP backend and jobs require no Node business execution; offline preparation tools may remain JavaScript. Pin Java 21 and the chosen supported Quarkus 3.x version at implementation refinement. A native-image build is not required by this proposal.

### acceptance

1. The in-scope backend builds and runs on Java 21 / Quarkus 3.x. A capability matrix accounts for all currently supported Node backend responsibilities and their Java replacements; omitted or unimplemented backlog work is identified explicitly.
2. The same supported frontend journeys pass against Quarkus using the agreed API contract. Authorization/expiry, signed-in offer entry/ownership, errors and source-unavailable cases follow the agreed behaviour, including the intentional OIDC/presenter changes. No frontend business rewrite is needed merely to change backend language.
3. Reference inputs preserve displayed values, eligibility, rankings/tie-breaks, allocations, explanations, order outcomes and persisted transitions within defined numeric tolerances. Prove the bounds and decision-sensitive edge cases; no silent rule changes or per-employee exceptions are introduced.
4. PostgreSQL integration proves competing claims, duplicate/retried commands, uncertain writes, expiry/reset and interrupted-work recovery preserve existing guarantees. Retained source/reference inputs remain readable and correct across the rehearsed cutover. Replacement-run records, active offers and pinned policy/quote references survive normal runtime restart; legacy operational-state migration is not required.
5. The Java runtime meets the adapter-completion acceptance below, including complete provider composition, separation of demo preparation and a connected substitution demonstration. Mock-backed journeys function through Java application services; API-compatible Node forwarding is identified as a temporary migration state.
6. Existing scenario/comparison sizes and a few simultaneous demo users demonstrate usable journeys/jobs within the selected Render resources. Record actual workload/resource results. Demonstrate release/readiness, rehearse the agreed fresh-state cutover and hand over retirement of the in-scope Node runtime through Gary's merge-triggered replacement. No old-deployment retention or rollback proof is required. Any required hosting-plan/cost change is explicit before provisioning; no performance improvement or production-scale capacity is claimed without evidence.

### validate

Reuse current business contracts, manual scenarios and decision fixtures as the behaviour baseline. Map Node and replacement API responses into equivalent journey/decision checks on isolated equivalent state; validate the new API against its agreed contract. Add Java service/repository checks where existing JavaScript tests exercise implementation directly. Use actual PostgreSQL for transaction/concurrency/restart evidence and replay business-provider refusal/uncertainty paths with realistic substitutes. Prove real mail delivery through the configured transport to an agreed test recipient and follow the offer through OIDC/ownership checks. Rehearse Render deployment and fresh-state startup on development state, then record hosted workload results and limitations. Prepare final-switch verification for Gary without performing his merge. Existing checks establish intended behaviour; they do not prove the Java implementation or require a new general validation framework.

**Boundary:** the port preserves implemented GCSP capabilities subject to the explicitly agreed OIDC/presenter changes, and introduces no new product rules, live BMW integration, database-engine change, AWS move, microservice split, native-image requirement or Used Cars backend migration. Java/Quarkus does not by itself prove production-platform compatibility or resolve the separately tracked performance/reliability work.

### Adapter completion and proof within E3

**Intent:** As the team integrating GCSP, we can connect an authorized external service by implementing its adapter and configuring the backend, while preserving the Angular API contract and the application's existing decision logic.

**Existing baseline, assessed 13 November:** [the adapter-readiness assessment](https://github.com/garyscarter-ibm/vehicle-matcher/blob/23f6ce3313916f41264c3157d70188d79287d511/docs/gcsp/adapter-readiness-assessment-2026-11-13.md) confirms substantial implementation and passing selected substitution/protocol tests. Employee/identity reads, vehicle evidence, policy/storage, remote manual/Buddy claims, ordering and mail already have boundaries. Remaining work includes full provider composition separated from demo preparation, remote offer acceptance/decline and connected replacement evidence. This workstream credits that existing work; it does not commission a new adapter architecture or claim every criterion starts unbuilt. Constructing a synthetic provider in the composition root is not itself a coupling defect.

#### decided / proposed scope

- Include remote offer acceptance/decline as a separate bounded Story within E3, as Gary confirmed during refinement. It completes a missing provider protocol rather than mechanical cleanup; preserve prior delivered Story exclusions. Prove the first Buddy journey with local substitutes, then complete the remote substitute and full transactional adapter proof before final migration acceptance.
- Inventory every external source and operation used by the implemented journeys. For each, identify the authoritative system, application-facing contract, present provider, source/provenance, capabilities and known live-service gaps. Reuse existing ports and contracts rather than introduce a parallel adapter framework.
- Cover reads, commands and relevant events/status reconciliation. “Fetch all data through adapters” alone would miss exclusive claims, order submission, uncertain writes, approvals and notifications.
- Select providers through trusted deployment/startup configuration. Remove required service-code edits merely to select an alternative provider; keep provider field names, transport and authentication inside its adapter. Dynamic presenter switching is unnecessary. No implicit switch to synthetic success when a live provider fails.
- Keep mock/recorded providers functional: they supply inputs and perform real scenario state transitions through the same application services. Recommendations, allocations and aggregates are computed from those inputs.
- Define required and optional capabilities honestly. Unsupported actions, absent facts, source delays and uncertain outcomes have explicit results that existing application services can handle. A replacement cannot fabricate authority that the upstream service does not provide.

Initial capability inventory to reconcile with the actual implementation:

| Boundary | Examples of information/actions | Ownership to preserve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity and employee context | Principal/roles, entitlement, drivers, current car/contract and available usage facts | Backend resolves the principal and enforces employee/resource access. |
| Scheme policy and reference inputs | Dated eligibility, allowance, points and approved assumptions | One PolicyService remains the application contract; internal policy storage need not become an external system. |
| Supply and stock | Inbound/released stock, release/status inputs, claim/reservation/release capabilities | Explicit authority for exact stock and exclusive holds; no competing upstream/local owner. |
| Vehicle evidence | Catalogue/specification, configuration/VIN relationships, imagery and available handbook data | Preserve exact identity, source/freshness and synthetic-identifier routing protections. |
| Ordering and lifecycle | Requests, status, approvals, documents, appointments and return outcomes used today | Preserve provider references, pending reconciliation and the actual commitment boundary. |
| Notifications | Captured delivery and available real transport outcomes | Notification delivery follows business state; transport success does not allocate a car. |

This is a coverage checklist, not a requirement for six services or six adapters, nor authorization to add new telemetry or implement every future integration.

#### acceptance

1. Every in-scope external read, action and event path is mapped to a backend port and selected adapter. Direct upstream calls, fixture imports and demo seeding cannot bypass that boundary in a live configuration. Application-owned state and derived results are separately identified.
2. In-scope providers can be selected through backend composition without changing Angular components, public API payloads or core application services. The same services handle synthetic, recorded and conforming external inputs.
3. Each required port has contract evidence for its supported operations and relevant failure/capability states. Existing contracts cover identity, units, missing/stale facts, provenance and command/reference semantics as applicable; do not invent generic fields that no consumer needs.
4. A substitution demonstration replaces providers at the backend boundary and replays representative read-only and transactional journeys. Changed source inputs change the computed recommendations/results. Refused, expired or uncertain commands remain truthful, and retries/reconciliation preserve exclusive claims and avoid duplicate external actions.
5. The inventory distinguishes **synthetic implementation**, **recorded/source-backed evidence**, **contract-tested replacement** and **authorized live integration verified**. Two test providers can prove interchangeability, but cannot establish that an unavailable BMW service supports the contract. Actual live activation requires the relevant service's authorized access and positive integration evidence.

#### validate

Reuse existing adapter, service, HTTP and journey checks. Exercise the actual runtime composition, not just constructors in isolation. Include at least an employee-context/stock-to-recommendation flow and a claim-to-order/status flow, plus the relevant failure/retry cases. For ports not used by those two journeys, retain focused contract evidence and an explicit coverage record. Keep fixture reset and synthetic-identifier protections isolated from any real integration. Contract mismatch or missing upstream capability is a recorded integration gap, not a passing mock test.

**Boundary:** this workstream establishes and proves replacement seams for existing capabilities. It does not commission every live BMW adapter, invent missing APIs, migrate hosting to AWS or establish production readiness. Its implementation and evidence belong to E3 alongside the Java port; actual live integrations remain separately scoped capabilities, including the existing live catalogue/imagery work.

## Shared confirmed migration contract

- Scope is GCSP only. Preserve implemented capabilities, business outcomes and visual design at the exact `gcsp-poc-dev` implementation-kickoff SHA, apart from the agreed OIDC/presenter changes. Record that SHA, routes/jobs/capabilities, retained artifact identities, workload and visual references at kickoff. Preserve Used Cars and shared consumers; unfinished backlog and later product changes stay separate. Legacy GCSP URL/API compatibility is unnecessary.
- Angular 21 owns screens/navigation and calls a separately buildable/deployable Java 21 / Quarkus 3.x API. Runtime/jobs use Java without invoking Node business execution; offline generators/trainers may remain JavaScript. Pin compatible exact versions, reconcile BMW standards when supplied and keep interim Render delivery. One repository and Render blueprint define separate frontend/API artifacts. Reuse unchanged compiled Angular bundles with deployment-supplied public API/OIDC settings and no embedded secrets.
- Use real test OAuth 2.0/OIDC browser login and JWT access tokens sent as `Authorization: Bearer`; backend validates signature/issuer/audience/lifetime and enforces roles/ownership. BMW activation follows available contracts/access. Employees and Greg act only through their own logins. Presenter controls clock/releases/scenarios/resets/faults/retry plus read-only inspection such as outbox/comparison; no impersonation or employee/Greg commands. Greg retains comparison commands.
- Renew authentication where supported; otherwise sign in and return to the authorized page with saved progress. Never automatically submit an unfinished order after recovery; require explicit confirmation. Sign-out clears app authentication and ends the provider session where supported so another account can sign in. New emailed offer links require sign-in/return and employee ownership.
- Gary creates the isolated Render dev environment from `gcsp-poc-dev`, with its own PostgreSQL database. Prefer existing hostnames without buying a domain; prove HTTPS/CORS/OIDC/link topology. Minimize cost and show measured options before any spending change; no tier is selected. Prove existing scenario/comparison sizes with a few simultaneous demo users.
- Retain source corpus, policy/reference versions, reusable trained models and agreed baseline comparison artifacts. Legacy employee/scenario state, sessions, active offers/orders, old emailed links and operational learning/comparison history may reset at final switch. Replacement-app state and newly issued links must survive ordinary compatible releases/restarts. Never reset the running app's database from dev.
- Select backend adapters at deployment/startup. Reuse existing ports; separate provider transport/shape/authentication and demo preparation from application services. No silent synthetic fallback, fabricated source facts or per-employee outcomes. Keep canonical PolicyService, exact vehicle identity, provenance, pinned quotes, exclusive authority, durable receipts, retries and truthful pending/refused/uncertain outcomes. Numeric tolerances must preserve displayed values, eligibility, ranking/tie-breaks and allocation/order outcomes.
- Delivery order: foundation → real sign-in/account → Buddy matching → real test email → signed-in acceptance → order/status with local substitutes first; then remaining capabilities and the remote/full transactional substitution proof before final acceptance. Both proofs use real test OIDC and actual email delivery through the configured mail adapter to an agreed test recipient. Captured outbox alone is insufficient. Test substitutes do not establish unavailable live BMW integration.
- Complete and validate continuously, with coherent commits and no interim human review gates. Gary checks the whole hosted dev build at the end, then performs the merge into `gcsp-poc` that triggers Render replacement. Downtime and immediate retirement are acceptable; no old-deployment retention, job-draining or deployment rollback rehearsal is required. Database transaction rollback and normal replacement-app recovery remain required.
- Settle persistence design early against Russell's FUCQ-408/FUCQ-409–425 objectives; deliver relevant persistence changes with Java. Completing the whole Node refactor is not a gate. Existing native acceptance/claims stay fixed and optional tuning remains separately prioritized. This publication does not modify those issues or claim Java work satisfies Node-specific acceptance.

Read `docs/gcsp/README.md`, `docs/gcsp/demo-brief.md` (binding adapter/purpose boundaries), `docs/gcsp/build-rules.md` (including demo delivery/scope control), `docs/gcsp/experience-quality.md`, `COMPONENTS.md` and `docs/gcsp/technical-readiness-2026-11-05.md` before pickup. Preserve the kickoff implementation's visual design. The existing reference in `docs/gcsp/screens/README.md` governs shell/header/sidebar/palette; use the current shared components and recorded approved implementation references for the body. UI and visible backend changes need actual rendered desktop/narrow, Safari/private-browsing, keyboard/focus and relevant CSP/accessibility evidence. Record affected loading/empty/unavailable/denied/stale/pending/success/expiry states as applicable; backend decision changes need corresponding presentation evidence. Shared changes require relevant Used Cars checks.

Reuse meaningful existing service/HTTP/journey/adapter scenarios; avoid a new generic validation framework. Run integrated Angular journeys against the actual Java API and native PostgreSQL for transaction/concurrency/restart evidence. Record real failed, skipped and unrun checks and limitations. Builds, fixtures, source inspection and diagrams do not establish integrated acceptance or live BMW access. Triage defects under the standing policy and keep claimed acceptance fixed.

Publication creates backlog records only: no claim, implementation, provisioning, deployment, reset, test email or final merge is started. Verify actual contracts/interfaces, active ownership and concrete technical blockers, then size or split oversized work before pickup. Jira dependency links alone are not admission gates. args.summary: Build and publish the static GCSP artifact
args.description:
Local migration Story: `E1.S03`; parent source label: `E1`.

### decided

Build Angular independently from the API in this repository. Use one Render blueprint with separate service/build definitions and deployment-supplied public configuration.

### acceptance

1. A complete static build contains required assets and runs without request-time Node HTML processing; build filters support independent frontend/API releases.
2. Different public API/OIDC settings work with unchanged compiled Angular bundle hashes. Cache, CSP and referrer behaviour follow the supported routes and identity flow.

### validate

Build/serve the artifact and compare bundle identities under two public configurations. Verify actual deployed headers, asset loading and independence from the API build.

## Scope detail and technical edge

Angular output, shared assets and required route assets build independently. Deployment supplies public API/OIDC configuration separately from compiled bundles; demonstrate different environment settings with unchanged Angular bundle hashes. Asset versioning, cache/CSP/referrer rules no longer depend on per-request Node HTML processing. The shared Render blueprint defines both services; build filters distinguish static and API releases from this repository.

E2's first build; do not commission a full legacy-page packaging rewrite. Q12–Q14, Q23, Q29.

## Shared confirmed migration contract

- Scope is GCSP only. Preserve implemented capabilities, business outcomes and visual design at the exact `gcsp-poc-dev` implementation-kickoff SHA, apart from the agreed OIDC/presenter changes. Record that SHA, routes/jobs/capabilities, retained artifact identities, workload and visual references at kickoff. Preserve Used Cars and shared consumers; unfinished backlog and later product changes stay separate. Legacy GCSP URL/API compatibility is unnecessary.
- Angular 21 owns screens/navigation and calls a separately buildable/deployable Java 21 / Quarkus 3.x API. Runtime/jobs use Java without invoking Node business execution; offline generators/trainers may remain JavaScript. Pin compatible exact versions, reconcile BMW standards when supplied and keep interim Render delivery. One repository and Render blueprint define separate frontend/API artifacts. Reuse unchanged compiled Angular bundles with deployment-supplied public API/OIDC settings and no embedded secrets.
- Use real test OAuth 2.0/OIDC browser login and JWT access tokens sent as `Authorization: Bearer`; backend validates signature/issuer/audience/lifetime and enforces roles/ownership. BMW activation follows available contracts/access. Employees and Greg act only through their own logins. Presenter controls clock/releases/scenarios/resets/faults/retry plus read-only inspection such as outbox/comparison; no impersonation or employee/Greg commands. Greg retains comparison commands.
- Renew authentication where supported; otherwise sign in and return to the authorized page with saved progress. Never automatically submit an unfinished order after recovery; require explicit confirmation. Sign-out clears app authentication and ends the provider session where supported so another account can sign in. New emailed offer links require sign-in/return and employee ownership.
- Gary creates the isolated Render dev environment from `gcsp-poc-dev`, with its own PostgreSQL database. Prefer existing hostnames without buying a domain; prove HTTPS/CORS/OIDC/link topology. Minimize cost and show measured options before any spending change; no tier is selected. Prove existing scenario/comparison sizes with a few simultaneous demo users.
- Retain source corpus, policy/reference versions, reusable trained models and agreed baseline comparison artifacts. Legacy employee/scenario state, sessions, active offers/orders, old emailed links and operational learning/comparison history may reset at final switch. Replacement-app state and newly issued links must survive ordinary compatible releases/restarts. Never reset the running app's database from dev.
- Select backend adapters at deployment/startup. Reuse existing ports; separate provider transport/shape/authentication and demo preparation from application services. No silent synthetic fallback, fabricated source facts or per-employee outcomes. Keep canonical PolicyService, exact vehicle identity, provenance, pinned quotes, exclusive authority, durable receipts, retries and truthful pending/refused/uncertain outcomes. Numeric tolerances must preserve displayed values, eligibility, ranking/tie-breaks and allocation/order outcomes.
- Delivery order: foundation → real sign-in/account → Buddy matching → real test email → signed-in acceptance → order/status with local substitutes first; then remaining capabilities and the remote/full transactional substitution proof before final acceptance. Both proofs use real test OIDC and actual email delivery through the configured mail adapter to an agreed test recipient. Captured outbox alone is insufficient. Test substitutes do not establish unavailable live BMW integration.
- Complete and validate continuously, with coherent commits and no interim human review gates. Gary checks the whole hosted dev build at the end, then performs the merge into `gcsp-poc` that triggers Render replacement. Downtime and immediate retirement are acceptable; no old-deployment retention, job-draining or deployment rollback rehearsal is required. Database transaction rollback and normal replacement-app recovery remain required.
- Settle persistence design early against Russell's FUCQ-408/FUCQ-409–425 objectives; deliver relevant persistence changes with Java. Completing the whole Node refactor is not a gate. Existing native acceptance/claims stay fixed and optional tuning remains separately prioritized. This publication does not modify those issues or claim Java work satisfies Node-specific acceptance.

## Binding delivery and experience references

Read `docs/gcsp/README.md`, `docs/gcsp/demo-brief.md` (binding adapter/purpose boundaries), `docs/gcsp/build-rules.md` (including demo delivery/scope control), `docs/gcsp/experience-quality.md`, `COMPONENTS.md` and `docs/gcsp/technical-readiness-2026-11-05.md` before pickup. Preserve the kickoff implementation's visual design. The existing reference in `docs/gcsp/screens/README.md` governs shell/header/sidebar/palette; use the current shared components and recorded approved implementation references for the body. UI and visible backend changes need actual rendered desktop/narrow, Safari/private-browsing, keyboard/focus and relevant CSP/accessibility evidence. Record affected loading/empty/unavailable/denied/stale/pending/success/expiry states as applicable; backend decision changes need corresponding presentation evidence. Shared changes require relevant Used Cars checks.

Reuse meaningful existing service/HTTP/journey/adapter scenarios; avoid a new generic validation framework. Run integrated Angular journeys against the actual Java API and native PostgreSQL for transaction/concurrency/restart evidence. Record real failed, skipped and unrun checks and limitations. Builds, fixtures, source inspection and diagrams do not establish integrated acceptance or live BMW access. Triage defects under the standing policy and keep claimed acceptance fixed.

Publication creates backlog records only: no claim, implementation, provisioning, deployment, reset, test email or final merge is started. Verify actual contracts/interfaces, active ownership and concrete technical blockers, then size or split oversized work before pickup. Jira dependency links alone are not admission gates. args.summary: Review and intentionally submit a manual selection
args.description:
Local migration Story: `E2.S05`; parent source label: `E2`.

### decided

Preserve current manual review, declarations and order handoff using E3.S10/S15. Submission remains an intentional employee action.

### acceptance

1. Claim, review/edit and submission retain the exact car, quoted terms, draft versions and required declarations.
2. Confirmed, pending, stale and refused submissions display actual backend state. Repeat entry/retry cannot invent confirmation or duplicate a request.

### validate

Replay claim-to-order against Java/PostgreSQL, including stale quotes, declaration failures and lost responses. Inspect review and resulting status; verify recovery requires unfinished-order confirmation.

## Scope detail and technical edge

Preserve claim, edit/review, declarations, quote/draft versions, confirmed/pending/refused submission and repeat-entry semantics through the real API.

Existing manual review/order contracts; E3.S10 and E3.S15. Q25, Q28.

## Shared confirmed migration contract

- Scope is GCSP only. Preserve implemented capabilities, business outcomes and visual design at the exact `gcsp-poc-dev` implementation-kickoff SHA, apart from the agreed OIDC/presenter changes. Record that SHA, routes/jobs/capabilities, retained artifact identities, workload and visual references at kickoff. Preserve Used Cars and shared consumers; unfinished backlog and later product changes stay separate. Legacy GCSP URL/API compatibility is unnecessary.
- Angular 21 owns screens/navigation and calls a separately buildable/deployable Java 21 / Quarkus 3.x API. Runtime/jobs use Java without invoking Node business execution; offline generators/trainers may remain JavaScript. Pin compatible exact versions, reconcile BMW standards when supplied and keep interim Render delivery. One repository and Render blueprint define separate frontend/API artifacts. Reuse unchanged compiled Angular bundles with deployment-supplied public API/OIDC settings and no embedded secrets.
- Use real test OAuth 2.0/OIDC browser login and JWT access tokens sent as `Authorization: Bearer`; backend validates signature/issuer/audience/lifetime and enforces roles/ownership. BMW activation follows available contracts/access. Employees and Greg act only through their own logins. Presenter controls clock/releases/scenarios/resets/faults/retry plus read-only inspection such as outbox/comparison; no impersonation or employee/Greg commands. Greg retains comparison commands.
- Renew authentication where supported; otherwise sign in and return to the authorized page with saved progress. Never automatically submit an unfinished order after recovery; require explicit confirmation. Sign-out clears app authentication and ends the provider session where supported so another account can sign in. New emailed offer links require sign-in/return and employee ownership.
- Gary creates the isolated Render dev environment from `gcsp-poc-dev`, with its own PostgreSQL database. Prefer existing hostnames without buying a domain; prove HTTPS/CORS/OIDC/link topology. Minimize cost and show measured options before any spending change; no tier is selected. Prove existing scenario/comparison sizes with a few simultaneous demo users.
- Retain source corpus, policy/reference versions, reusable trained models and agreed baseline comparison artifacts. Legacy employee/scenario state, sessions, active offers/orders, old emailed links and operational learning/comparison history may reset at final switch. Replacement-app state and newly issued links must survive ordinary compatible releases/restarts. Never reset the running app's database from dev.
- Select backend adapters at deployment/startup. Reuse existing ports; separate provider transport/shape/authentication and demo preparation from application services. No silent synthetic fallback, fabricated source facts or per-employee outcomes. Keep canonical PolicyService, exact vehicle identity, provenance, pinned quotes, exclusive authority, durable receipts, retries and truthful pending/refused/uncertain outcomes. Numeric tolerances must preserve displayed values, eligibility, ranking/tie-breaks and allocation/order outcomes.
- Delivery order: foundation → real sign-in/account → Buddy matching → real test email → signed-in acceptance → order/status with local substitutes first; then remaining capabilities and the remote/full transactional substitution proof before final acceptance. Test substitutes do not establish unavailable live BMW integration.

args.summary: Track the existing order and lifecycle journey
args.description:
Local migration Story: `E2.S08`; parent source label: `E2`.

### decided

Consume E3.S17–S20 status/actions. Preserve only implemented kickoff scope; appointment/return plans do not themselves complete physical events.

### acceptance

1. Supported approval, document, readiness, appointment and return states/actions reflect the provider and employee authority.
2. Ownership, pending/refused work and current-car relationships remain accurate through reload and supported transitions.

### validate

Replay the implemented lifecycle scenarios through Java and inspect progress/action states. Confirm plans versus completed outcomes and missing-provider refusals; split independently owned UI capability before pickup if oversized.

## Scope detail and technical edge

Display actual pending/approval/document/readiness/appointment/return states and supported actions, preserving existing scope and current-car relationship rules. Inventory may split this by independently owned lifecycle capability before pickup.

Existing progress/lifecycle contracts; E3.S17–S20. Q05–Q06, Q25.

## Shared confirmed migration contract

- Scope is GCSP only. Preserve implemented capabilities, business outcomes and visual design at the exact `gcsp-poc-dev` implementation-kickoff SHA, apart from the agreed OIDC/presenter changes. Record that SHA, routes/jobs/capabilities, retained artifact identities, workload and visual references at kickoff. Preserve Used Cars and shared consumers; unfinished backlog and later product changes stay separate. Legacy GCSP URL/API compatibility is unnecessary.
- Angular 21 owns screens/navigation and calls a separately buildable/deployable Java 21 / Quarkus 3.x API. Runtime/jobs use Java without invoking Node business execution; offline generators/trainers may remain JavaScript. Pin compatible exact versions, reconcile BMW standards when supplied and keep interim Render delivery. One repository and Render blueprint define separate frontend/API artifacts. Reuse unchanged compiled Angular bundles with deployment-supplied public API/OIDC settings and no embedded secrets.
- Use real test OAuth 2.0/OIDC browser login and JWT access tokens sent as `Authorization: Bearer`; backend validates signature/issuer/audience/lifetime and enforces roles/ownership. BMW activation follows available contracts/access. Employees and Greg act only through their own logins. Presenter controls clock/releases/scenarios/resets/faults/retry plus read-only inspection such as outbox/comparison; no impersonation or employee/Greg commands. Greg retains comparison commands.
- Renew authentication where supported; otherwise sign in and return to the authorized page with saved progress. Never automatically submit an unfinished order after recovery; require explicit confirmation. Sign-out clears app authentication and ends the provider session where supported so another account can sign in. New emailed offer links require sign-in/return and employee ownership.
- Gary creates the isolated Render dev environment from `gcsp-poc-dev`, with its own PostgreSQL database. Prefer existing hostnames without buying a domain; prove HTTPS/CORS/OIDC/link topology. Minimize cost and show measured options before any spending change; no tier is selected. Prove existing scenario/comparison sizes with a few simultaneous demo users.
- Retain source corpus, policy/reference versions, reusable trained models and agreed baseline comparison artifacts. Legacy employee/scenario state, sessions, active offers/orders, old emailed links and operational learning/comparison history may reset at final switch. Replacement-app state and newly issued links must survive ordinary compatible releases/restarts. Never reset the running app's database from dev.
- Select backend adapters at deployment/startup. Reuse existing ports; separate provider transport/shape/authentication and demo preparation from application services. No silent synthetic fallback, fabricated source facts or per-employee outcomes. Keep canonical PolicyService, exact vehicle identity, provenance, pinned quotes, exclusive authority, durable receipts, retries and truthful pending/refused/uncertain outcomes. Numeric tolerances must preserve displayed values, eligibility, ranking/tie-breaks and allocation/order outcomes.
- Delivery order: foundation → real sign-in/account → Buddy matching → real test email → signed-in acceptance → order/status with local substitutes first; then remaining capabilities and the remote/full transactional substitution proof before final acceptance. Both proofs use real test OIDC and actual email delivery through the configured mail adapter to an agreed test recipient. Captured outbox alone is insufficient. Test substitutes do not establish unavailable live BMW integration.
- Complete and validate continuously, with coherent commits and no interim human review gates. Gary checks the whole hosted dev build at the end, then performs the merge into `gcsp-poc` that triggers Render replacement. Downtime and immediate retirement are acceptable; no old-deployment retention, job-draining or deployment rollback rehearsal is required. Database transaction rollback and normal replacement-app recovery remain required.
- Settle persistence design early against Russell's FUCQ-408/FUCQ-409–425 objectives; deliver relevant persistence changes with Java. Completing the whole Node refactor is not a gate. Existing native acceptance/claims stay fixed and optional tuning remains separately prioritized. This publication does not modify those issues or claim Java work satisfies Node-specific acceptance.

Preserve the kickoff implementation's visual design. The existing reference in `docs/gcsp/screens/README.md` governs shell/header/sidebar/palette; use the current shared components and recorded approved implementation references for the body. UI and visible backend changes need actual rendered desktop/narrow, Safari/private-browsing, keyboard/focus and relevant CSP/accessibility evidence. Record affected loading/empty/unavailable/denied/stale/pending/success/expiry states as applicable; backend decision changes need corresponding presentation evidence. Shared changes require relevant Used Cars checks.

Reuse meaningful existing service/HTTP/journey/adapter scenarios; avoid a new generic validation framework. Run integrated Angular journeys against the actual Java API and native PostgreSQL for transaction/concurrency/restart evidence. Record real failed, skipped and unrun checks and limitations. Builds, fixtures, source inspection and diagrams do not establish integrated acceptance or live BMW access. Triage defects under the standing policy and keep claimed acceptance fixed.

Publication creates backlog records only: no claim, implementation, provisioning, deployment, reset, test email or final merge is started. args.description:
Local migration Story: `E2.S15`; parent source label: `E2`.

### decided

Finish after capability/route parity. Angular owns the final GCSP frontend; preserve Used Cars and supported shared consumers.

### acceptance

### validate

## Shared confirmed migration contract

- Scope is GCSP only. Preserve implemented capabilities, business outcomes and visual design at the exact `gcsp-poc-dev` implementation-kickoff SHA, apart from the agreed OIDC/presenter changes. Record that SHA, routes/jobs/capabilities, retained artifact identities, workload and visual references at kickoff. Preserve Used Cars and shared consumers; unfinished backlog and later product changes stay separate. Legacy GCSP URL/API compatibility is unnecessary.
- Angular 21 owns screens/navigation and calls a separately buildable/deployable Java 21 / Quarkus 3.x API. Runtime/jobs use Java without invoking Node business execution; offline generators/trainers may remain JavaScript. Pin compatible exact versions, reconcile BMW standards when supplied and keep interim Render delivery. One repository and Render blueprint define separate frontend/API artifacts. Reuse unchanged compiled Angular bundles with deployment-supplied public API/OIDC settings and no embedded secrets.
- Use real test OAuth 2.0/OIDC browser login and JWT access tokens sent as `Authorization: Bearer`; backend validates signature/issuer/audience/lifetime and enforces roles/ownership. args.summary: Persist state in isolated development PostgreSQL
args.description:
Local migration Story: `E3.S03`; parent source label: `E3`.

### decided

Use the separate dev database and agreed operational reset. Settle the persistence design early against FUCQ-419–425 objectives; preserve transaction semantics without copying the Node whole-run snapshot/diff implementation into Java by default. Full Node optimization delivery is not a prerequisite.

### acceptance

1. Persist application state, command receipts and authority across normal restart with atomic mutations, version/concurrency checks and honest uncertain outcomes. Identify the selected SQL/schema and freshness strategy.
2. Verify actual connection/reset isolation from the running app. Record how targeted reads/writes, reference evidence and reset work align with existing database Stories, and which optimization evidence remains separate.

### validate

Use native PostgreSQL for commit/rollback, competing instances, failed version checks, idempotent replay, uncertain commit and restart. Inspect representative SQL/query scope; demonstrate a dev reset leaves the running database unchanged. Follow the alignment record for distinct performance acceptance.

## Scope detail and technical edge

Configure the blueprint's own development database; preserve new-app state, command records and required consistency across restart; reset only authorized development state. Verify connection targets and demonstrate a dev reset leaves the running app's database unchanged. Reconcile FUCQ-419–425 before fixing the Java persistence design, avoiding a mechanical port of broad whole-run snapshot/diff work. Record distinct optimization scope/evidence rather than absorbing the whole performance Epic.

PostgreSQL repository contract and confirmed separate database. Q12, Q27, Q37–Q38; FUCQ-408 alignment.

## Shared confirmed migration contract

- Scope is GCSP only. Preserve implemented capabilities, business outcomes and visual design at the exact `gcsp-poc-dev` implementation-kickoff SHA, apart from the agreed OIDC/presenter changes. Record that SHA, routes/jobs/capabilities, retained artifact identities, workload and visual references at kickoff. Preserve Used Cars and shared consumers; unfinished backlog and later product changes stay separate. Legacy GCSP URL/API compatibility is unnecessary.
- Angular 21 owns screens/navigation and calls a separately buildable/deployable Java 21 / Quarkus 3.x API. Runtime/jobs use Java without invoking Node business execution; offline generators/trainers may remain JavaScript. Pin compatible exact versions, reconcile BMW standards when supplied and keep interim Render delivery. One repository and Render blueprint define separate frontend/API artifacts. Reuse unchanged compiled Angular bundles with deployment-supplied public API/OIDC settings and no embedded secrets.
- Use real test OAuth 2.0/OIDC browser login and JWT access tokens sent as `Authorization: Bearer`; backend validates signature/issuer/audience/lifetime and enforces roles/ownership. BMW activation follows available contracts/access. Employees and Greg act only through their own logins. Presenter controls clock/releases/scenarios/resets/faults/retry plus read-only inspection such as outbox/comparison; no impersonation or employee/Greg commands. Greg retains comparison commands.
- Renew authentication where supported; otherwise sign in and return to the authorized page with saved progress. Never automatically submit an unfinished order after recovery; require explicit confirmation. Sign-out clears app authentication and ends the provider session where supported so another account can sign in. New emailed offer links require sign-in/return and employee ownership.
- Gary creates the isolated Render dev environment from `gcsp-poc-dev`, with its own PostgreSQL database. Prefer existing hostnames without buying a domain; prove HTTPS/CORS/OIDC/link topology. Minimize cost and show measured options before any spending change; no tier is selected. Prove existing scenario/comparison sizes with a few simultaneous demo users.
- Retain source corpus, policy/reference versions, reusable trained models and agreed baseline comparison artifacts. Legacy employee/scenario state, sessions, active offers/orders, old emailed links and operational learning/comparison history may reset at final switch. Replacement-app state and newly issued links must survive ordinary compatible releases/restarts. Never reset the running app's database from dev.
- Select backend adapters at deployment/startup. Reuse existing ports; separate provider transport/shape/authentication and demo preparation from application services. No silent synthetic fallback, fabricated source facts or per-employee outcomes. Keep canonical PolicyService, exact vehicle identity, provenance, pinned quotes, exclusive authority, durable receipts, retries and truthful pending/refused/uncertain outcomes. Numeric tolerances must preserve displayed values, eligibility, ranking/tie-breaks and allocation/order outcomes.
- Delivery order: foundation → real sign-in/account → Buddy matching → real test email → signed-in acceptance → order/status with local substitutes first; then remaining capabilities and the remote/full transactional substitution proof before final acceptance. Both proofs use real test OIDC and actual email delivery through the configured mail adapter to an agreed test recipient. Captured outbox alone is insufficient. Test substitutes do not establish unavailable live BMW integration.
- Complete and validate continuously, with coherent commits and no interim human review gates. Gary checks the whole hosted dev build at the end, then performs the merge into `gcsp-poc` that triggers Render replacement. Downtime and immediate retirement are acceptable; no old-deployment retention, job-draining or deployment rollback rehearsal is required. Database transaction rollback and normal replacement-app recovery remain required.
- Settle persistence design early against Russell's FUCQ-408/FUCQ-409–425 objectives; deliver relevant persistence changes with Java. Completing the whole Node refactor is not a gate. Existing native acceptance/claims stay fixed and optional tuning remains separately prioritized. This publication does not modify those issues or claim Java work satisfies Node-specific acceptance.

## Binding delivery and experience references

Read `docs/gcsp/README.md`, `docs/gcsp/demo-brief.md` (binding adapter/purpose boundaries), `docs/gcsp/build-rules.md` (including demo delivery/scope control), `docs/gcsp/experience-quality.md`, `COMPONENTS.md` and `docs/gcsp/technical-readiness-2026-11-05.md` before pickup. Preserve the kickoff implementation's visual design. The existing reference in `docs/gcsp/screens/README.md` governs shell/header/sidebar/palette; use the current shared components and recorded approved implementation references for the body. UI and visible backend changes need actual rendered desktop/narrow, Safari/private-browsing, keyboard/focus and relevant CSP/accessibility evidence. Record affected loading/empty/unavailable/denied/stale/pending/success/expiry states as applicable; backend decision changes need corresponding presentation evidence. Shared changes require relevant Used Cars checks.

Reuse meaningful existing service/HTTP/journey/adapter scenarios; avoid a new generic validation framework. Run integrated Angular journeys against the actual Java API and native PostgreSQL for transaction/concurrency/restart evidence. Record real failed, skipped and unrun checks and limitations. Builds, fixtures, source inspection and diagrams do not establish integrated acceptance or live BMW access. Triage defects under the standing policy and keep claimed acceptance fixed.

Publication creates backlog records only: no claim, implementation, provisioning, deployment, reset, test email or final merge is started. args.summary: Apply local offer decisions and follow-up
args.description:
Local migration Story: `E3.S13`; parent source label: `E3`.

### decided

Preserve existing local accept/decline, source conversion, current eligibility versus retained quote, typed feedback and supported follow-up. E3.S14 owns the missing remote protocol.

### acceptance

1. Authorized explicit decisions revalidate current state, atomically preserve custody/order-conversion guarantees and produce the actual outcome once.
2. Conflicts, expiry, replay and refused/pending downstream work remain truthful. Decline releases authority under existing rules and permits only supported follow-up.

### validate

Replay local accept/decline, duplicate/conflicting commands, stale quotes/versions, expiry and conversion failure against PostgreSQL. Inspect resulting offer/activity/order states and historical receipts.

## Scope detail and technical edge

Preserve local accept/decline, custody/order-conversion boundary, idempotency, expiry, feedback and supported follow-up. API outcomes remain truthful through pending or refused downstream work.

Existing decision/follow-up/conversion contracts. Q28, Q30.

## Shared confirmed migration contract

- Scope is GCSP only. Preserve implemented capabilities, business outcomes and visual design at the exact `gcsp-poc-dev` implementation-kickoff SHA, apart from the agreed OIDC/presenter changes. Record that SHA, routes/jobs/capabilities, retained artifact identities, workload and visual references at kickoff. Preserve Used Cars and shared consumers; unfinished backlog and later product changes stay separate. Legacy GCSP URL/API compatibility is unnecessary.
- Angular 21 owns screens/navigation and calls a separately buildable/deployable Java 21 / Quarkus 3.x API. Runtime/jobs use Java without invoking Node business execution; offline generators/trainers may remain JavaScript. Pin compatible exact versions, reconcile BMW standards when supplied and keep interim Render delivery. One repository and Render blueprint define separate frontend/API artifacts. Reuse unchanged compiled Angular bundles with deployment-supplied public API/OIDC settings and no embedded secrets.
- Use real test OAuth 2.0/OIDC browser login and JWT access tokens sent as `Authorization: Bearer`; backend validates signature/issuer/audience/lifetime and enforces roles/ownership. BMW activation follows available contracts/access. Employees and Greg act only through their own logins. Presenter controls clock/releases/scenarios/resets/faults/retry plus read-only inspection such as outbox/comparison; no impersonation or employee/Greg commands. Greg retains comparison commands.
- Renew authentication where supported; otherwise sign in and return to the authorized page with saved progress. Never automatically submit an unfinished order after recovery; require explicit confirmation. Sign-out clears app authentication and ends the provider session where supported so another account can sign in. New emailed offer links require sign-in/return and employee ownership.
- Gary creates the isolated Render dev environment from `gcsp-poc-dev`, with its own PostgreSQL database. Prefer existing hostnames without buying a domain; prove HTTPS/CORS/OIDC/link topology. Minimize cost and show measured options before any spending change; no tier is selected. Prove existing scenario/comparison sizes with a few simultaneous demo users.
- Retain source corpus, policy/reference versions, reusable trained models and agreed baseline comparison artifacts. Legacy employee/scenario state, sessions, active offers/orders, old emailed links and operational learning/comparison history may reset at final switch. Replacement-app state and newly issued links must survive ordinary compatible releases/restarts. Never reset the running app's database from dev.
- Select backend adapters at deployment/startup. Reuse existing ports; separate provider transport/shape/authentication and demo preparation from application services. No silent synthetic fallback, fabricated source facts or per-employee outcomes. Keep canonical PolicyService, exact vehicle identity, provenance, pinned quotes, exclusive authority, durable receipts, retries and truthful pending/refused/uncertain outcomes. Numeric tolerances must preserve displayed values, eligibility, ranking/tie-breaks and allocation/order outcomes.
- Delivery order: foundation → real sign-in/account → Buddy matching → real test email → signed-in acceptance → order/status with local substitutes first; then remaining capabilities and the remote/full transactional substitution proof before final acceptance. Both proofs use real test OIDC and actual email delivery through the configured mail adapter to an agreed test recipient. Captured outbox alone is insufficient. Test substitutes do not establish unavailable live BMW integration.
- Complete and validate continuously, with coherent commits and no interim human review gates. Gary checks the whole hosted dev build at the end, then performs the merge into `gcsp-poc` that triggers Render replacement. Downtime and immediate retirement are acceptable; no old-deployment retention, job-draining or deployment rollback rehearsal is required. Database transaction rollback and normal replacement-app recovery remain required.
- Settle persistence design early against Russell's FUCQ-408/FUCQ-409–425 objectives; deliver relevant persistence changes with Java. Completing the whole Node refactor is not a gate. Existing native acceptance/claims stay fixed and optional tuning remains separately prioritized. This publication does not modify those issues or claim Java work satisfies Node-specific acceptance.

## Binding delivery and experience references

Read `docs/gcsp/README.md`, `docs/gcsp/demo-brief.md` (binding adapter/purpose boundaries), `docs/gcsp/build-rules.md` (including demo delivery/scope control), `docs/gcsp/experience-quality.md`, `COMPONENTS.md` and `docs/gcsp/technical-readiness-2026-11-05.md` before pickup. Preserve the kickoff implementation's visual design. The existing reference in `docs/gcsp/screens/README.md` governs shell/header/sidebar/palette; use the current shared components and recorded approved implementation references for the body. UI and visible backend changes need actual rendered desktop/narrow, Safari/private-browsing, keyboard/focus and relevant CSP/accessibility evidence. Record affected loading/empty/unavailable/denied/stale/pending/success/expiry states as applicable; backend decision changes need corresponding presentation evidence. Shared changes require relevant Used Cars checks.

Reuse meaningful existing service/HTTP/journey/adapter scenarios; avoid a new generic validation framework. Run integrated Angular journeys against the actual Java API and native PostgreSQL for transaction/concurrency/restart evidence. Record real failed, skipped and unrun checks and limitations. Builds, fixtures, source inspection and diagrams do not establish integrated acceptance or live BMW access. Triage defects under the standing policy and keep claimed acceptance fixed.

Publication creates backlog records only: no claim, implementation, provisioning, deployment, reset, test email or final merge is started. Verify actual contracts/interfaces, active ownership and concrete technical blockers, then size or split oversized work before pickup. Jira dependency links alone are not admission gates. No estimates or assignments are invented here.

2. Prove real delivery through the configured adapter to the agreed test recipient and the OIDC/employee-owned offer journey. Outbox capture alone is insufficient.

### validate

Exercise capture, transport refusal/retry and state-before-notification ordering, then record bounded real mail receipt and browser return. Keep credentials outside artifacts and comparison runs free of outbound email.

## Scope detail and technical edge

Preserve the outbox/message/offer-link contract, capture mode, available Brevo transport, retries and state-before-notification ordering. Prove actual delivery through the configured adapter to an agreed test recipient, including the signed-in employee-owned offer journey.

Existing notify/mail configuration; sender/recipient details agreed for future validation. Q16, Q31, Q34.

## Shared confirmed migration contract

- Scope is GCSP only. Preserve implemented capabilities, business outcomes and visual design at the exact `gcsp-poc-dev` implementation-kickoff SHA, apart from the agreed OIDC/presenter changes. Record that SHA, routes/jobs/capabilities, retained artifact identities, workload and visual references at kickoff. Preserve Used Cars and shared consumers; unfinished backlog and later product changes stay separate. Legacy GCSP URL/API compatibility is unnecessary.
- Angular 21 owns screens/navigation and calls a separately buildable/deployable Java 21 / Quarkus 3.x API. Runtime/jobs use Java without invoking Node business execution; offline generators/trainers may remain JavaScript. Pin compatible exact versions, reconcile BMW standards when supplied and keep interim Render delivery. One repository and Render blueprint define separate frontend/API artifacts. Reuse unchanged compiled Angular bundles with deployment-supplied public API/OIDC settings and no embedded secrets.
- Use real test OAuth 2.0/OIDC browser login and JWT access tokens sent as `Authorization: Bearer`; backend validates signature/issuer/audience/lifetime and enforces roles/ownership. BMW activation follows available contracts/access. Employees and Greg act only through their own logins. Presenter controls clock/releases/scenarios/resets/faults/retry plus read-only inspection such as outbox/comparison; no impersonation or employee/Greg commands. Greg retains comparison commands.
- Renew authentication where supported; otherwise sign in and return to the authorized page with saved progress. args.summary: Consume learned artifacts and capture new learning records
args.description:
Local migration Story: `E3.S23`; parent source label: `E3`.

### decided

Retain reusable trained models and active model identity/features/inference. Operational learning history may reset; useful offline training/preparation may remain JavaScript.

### acceptance

1. Java consumes the documented model artifact/version and reproduces required forecasts/uncertainty within defined outcome-preserving numeric bounds, without Node runtime execution.
2. Implemented new-run learning records retain actual exposure/outcome provenance; unknown historical observations and synthetic evaluation limits remain explicit.

### validate

Verify artifact identities and cross-language feature/inference/reference cases, including missing/corrupt models and new record producers. Inspect downstream forecast/explanation results; offline artifact generation alone is insufficient.

## Scope detail and technical edge

Retain reusable trained models and implemented new-run record capture, active model identity/features/inference, forecast uncertainty and source/evaluation limits. Old operational learning history may reset. Offline preparation may remain JavaScript; document output format/version and consume artifacts from Java without Node.

Existing learned-model/forecast contracts. Q26, Q28–Q29, Q36.

## Shared confirmed migration contract

- Scope is GCSP only. Preserve implemented capabilities, business outcomes and visual design at the exact `gcsp-poc-dev` implementation-kickoff SHA, apart from the agreed OIDC/presenter changes. Record that SHA, routes/jobs/capabilities, retained artifact identities, workload and visual references at kickoff. Preserve Used Cars and shared consumers; unfinished backlog and later product changes stay separate. Legacy GCSP URL/API compatibility is unnecessary.
- Angular 21 owns screens/navigation and calls a separately buildable/deployable Java 21 / Quarkus 3.x API. Runtime/jobs use Java without invoking Node business execution; offline generators/trainers may remain JavaScript. Pin compatible exact versions, reconcile BMW standards when supplied and keep interim Render delivery. One repository and Render blueprint define separate frontend/API artifacts. Reuse unchanged compiled Angular bundles with deployment-supplied public API/OIDC settings and no embedded secrets.
- Use real test OAuth 2.0/OIDC browser login and JWT access tokens sent as `Authorization: Bearer`; backend validates signature/issuer/audience/lifetime and enforces roles/ownership. BMW activation follows available contracts/access. Employees and Greg act only through their own logins. Presenter controls clock/releases/scenarios/resets/faults/retry plus read-only inspection such as outbox/comparison; no impersonation or employee/Greg commands. Greg retains comparison commands.
- Renew authentication where supported; otherwise sign in and return to the authorized page with saved progress. Never automatically submit an unfinished order after recovery; require explicit confirmation. Sign-out clears app authentication and ends the provider session where supported so another account can sign in. New emailed offer links require sign-in/return and employee ownership.
- Gary creates the isolated Render dev environment from `gcsp-poc-dev`, with its own PostgreSQL database. Prefer existing hostnames without buying a domain; prove HTTPS/CORS/OIDC/link topology. Minimize cost and show measured options before any spending change; no tier is selected. Prove existing scenario/comparison sizes with a few simultaneous demo users.
- Retain source corpus, policy/reference versions, reusable trained models and agreed baseline comparison artifacts. Legacy employee/scenario state, sessions, active offers/orders, old emailed links and operational learning/comparison history may reset at final switch. Replacement-app state and newly issued links must survive ordinary compatible releases/restarts. Never reset the running app's database from dev.
- Select backend adapters at deployment/startup. Reuse existing ports; separate provider transport/shape/authentication and demo preparation from application services. No silent synthetic fallback, fabricated source facts or per-employee outcomes. Keep canonical PolicyService, exact vehicle identity, provenance, pinned quotes, exclusive authority, durable receipts, retries and truthful pending/refused/uncertain outcomes. Numeric tolerances must preserve displayed values, eligibility, ranking/tie-breaks and allocation/order outcomes.
- Delivery order: foundation → real sign-in/account → Buddy matching → real test email → signed-in acceptance → order/status with local substitutes first; then remaining capabilities and the remote/full transactional substitution proof before final acceptance. Test substitutes do not establish unavailable live BMW integration.
- Complete and validate continuously, with coherent commits and no interim human review gates. Gary checks the whole hosted dev build at the end, then performs the merge into `gcsp-poc` that triggers Render replacement. Downtime and immediate retirement are acceptable; no old-deployment retention, job-draining or deployment rollback rehearsal is required. Database transaction rollback and normal replacement-app recovery remain required.
- Settle persistence design early against Russell's FUCQ-408/FUCQ-409–425 objectives; deliver relevant persistence changes with Java. Completing the whole Node refactor is not a gate. Existing native acceptance/claims stay fixed and optional tuning remains separately prioritized. This publication does not modify those issues or claim Java work satisfies Node-specific acceptance.

The existing reference in `docs/gcsp/screens/README.md` governs shell/header/sidebar/palette; use the current shared components and recorded approved implementation references for the body. UI and visible backend changes need actual rendered desktop/narrow, Safari/private-browsing, keyboard/focus and relevant CSP/accessibility evidence. Shared changes require relevant Used Cars checks.
